notes.title: Gentlymad Studios Closing - Message to the community
notes.content:
[h3][b][i]A message from Stefan Marcinek, CEO and Founder of Assemble Entertainment
[/i][/b]
[/h3][p align="justify"]Today I have to share news I never wanted to write: Gentlymad Studios will close at the end of September 2025.
[/p][p align="justify"]For more than ten years, this team has been more than just a development studio. They've been friends, collaborators, and dreamers. From In Between to Pizza Connection 3 and the Endzone series, they put heart, humor, and incredible talent into everything they made.
[/p][p align="justify"]Endzone 2 had a journey as challenging as the world it's set in. The Early Access launch brought unexpected difficulties: low sales, mixed reviews, and some very hard conversations. But as Stephan Wirth said, “When criticism rolled in, we didn't retreat.” The team listened, improved, and kept going right until the end. I'll never regret that fight.
[/p][p align="justify"]In the end, those efforts couldn't sustain the studio. It's heartbreaking for the team, the players, and for me personally.
[/p][p align="justify"]Thank you to everyone who worked at Gentlymad, and to everyone who played their games, whether you discovered them in a post-apocalyptic wasteland or while running a pizza empire. The people behind these games made them possible, and I’m proud to have worked alongside them.
[/p][h3][i][b]Here's to each of them:[/b][/i][/h3][p]
[b]Daniel Denne [/b]- Art Lead, Co-Founder[b]
Matthias Guntrum [/b]- Project Lead, Co-Founder[b]
Stephan Wirth[/b] - Experience & Project Lead, Co-Founder[b]
Wolfgang Reichardt[/b] - Technical Lead, Co-Founder[/p][p]
[b]Anselm Kegel[/b] - Programmer
[b]Benedict Wolf[/b] - Management Assistant
[b]Constantin Blum[/b] - Design Lead
[b]Etienne Miller[/b] - UI Artist, UI Concepting
[b]Jonas Albrecht[/b] - Technical Artist, Music Composer, Cinematic Artist
[b]Kai Mergener[/b] - Material and Environment Artist
[b]Markus Pohl[/b] - Technical Artist
[b]Sebastian Louven[/b] - 3D Art Generalist
[b]Simone Rus-Denne[/b] - Concept Artist & 3D Art Generalist
[b]Stefan Treffeisen[/b] - Programmer
[b]Thomas Trocha[/b] - Programmer
[b]Tim Johannsen[/b] - Writer, Content Artist
[b]Yannick Edler von Hößle[/b] - 3D Art Generalist
[/p][p][b]Alexandra Rossinskaya[/b] - Intern, Concept Art
[b]Alina Sommer[/b] - Intern Technical Artist
[b]Dario Falcke[/b] - Intern
[b]Jana Mößner[/b] - Intern Technical Artist, Tooling
[b]Tessa Benz[/b] - Intern
[b]Timo Eberl[/b] - Programming, Technical Art
[b]Vanessa Voge[/b] - Intern UI Design[/p][p]
[b]So to everyone who played our games, gave feedback, or supported us in any way: Thank you.[/b][/p][p]- Stefan Marcinek (CEO of Assemble Entertainment & Gentlymad Studios) [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png"][/img][/p][h3][b][i]And now, I’d like to leave the final words to the people who brought these games to life: the Gentlymad Studios team themselves[/i][/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png"][/img][/p][h3]
[b]Dear survivors,[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We have some bittersweet news to share: Gentlymad Studios is closing down. This isn’t an easy message to write, but we wanted you to hear it directly from us.[/p][p][/p][p]Since founding the studio in 2014, we’ve been lucky enough to create games like In Between, Pizza Connection 3, and of course Endzone - A World Apart. With Endzone 2, we dreamed even bigger. It didn’t start where we hoped, but thanks to your feedback and support, we worked tirelessly through Early Access to bring it to a place we can truly be proud of.[/p][p]
Over the past months, we felt we were at a tipping point - more and more players were beginning to see the vision we had for the game. Not being able to carry it further is heartbreaking for us, but we’re deeply proud of how far it has come.[/p][p]
Through all the ups and downs, it was you, our players, who made this journey so meaningful. Every comment, every idea, every survival story you shared kept us going. You weren’t just our audience - you were part of the team.[/p][p][/p][p]From the bottom of our hearts: thank you for believing in us, for playing our games, and for helping shape them into what they became. Though Gentlymad Studios is coming to an end, the worlds we built together will live on through you.[/p][h3]
[b]With love and gratitude, 💚[/b][/h3][h3][b]The Gentlymad Studios Team[/b][/h3]

notes.title: Behind-the-scenes of Expeditions in Endzone 2 - Part 2
notes.content:
[h3]Survivors![/h3]
As promised, we are back for Part 2 😎

Today, we are diving deeper into the technical and visual challenges behind the game’s expedition system.

Let's jump straight into it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1053429d21f6ebf6f5022d15ac8f293cee38358c.png[/img]
[h1]Underground Expeditions: 
Welcome to the Endzone![/h1]

One of the most ambitious changes? The new [b]underground expeditions[/b], including the [b]Endzone bunker system[/b], a name-giving location in the world’s lore.
These levels posed unique technical challenges.
“The systems are optimized for the above-ground world. Underground, we had to create an illusion, and spawn another world and hide it from view,” one developer explained.

It would definitely break the immersion if as a player, you noticed you were actually floating 1,000 meters up in the air, above the map..!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/5b581e48dec7452a240a266006e07d2fee18ab85.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1053429d21f6ebf6f5022d15ac8f293cee38358c.png[/img]
[h2]Lighting and textures[/h2]

The illusion of being underground relied heavily on visual trickery and precise technical work.

Lighting, for example, had to be reworked entirely to fit these new locations.
When designing those expeditions, one unexpected challenge popped up: the sun. 
You’d think in a bunker 1,000 meters below the surface, the sun wouldn’t be much of a problem… but as you now know, the bunker isn’t [b]actually[/b] below the ground, and the sun is deeply baked into Endzone 2’s rendering system.

So, since removing it wasn’t exactly the best option, the devs decided instead to freeze it at a certain position and tint it a cold, unnatural gray-purple, and put it 90 degrees on top at its perfect zenith to avoid any shadows that would look weird underground!

But then, what happens to areas the player can’t reach or see? What should the walls of the world and the areas around the underground buildings themselves look like?
Well, you guessed it, here again the team had to experiment with textures, starting with inspiration from Fallout 2: raw earth textures that worked well for low-res pixel art. 
But in Endzone 2, they didn’t hold up. Eventually, the devs landed on a solution: perfectly black textures extracted from the very few perfectly black pixels available, and enhanced with carefully placed lighting. The goal? Darkness that felt real, not shiny, flat, or fake.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1053429d21f6ebf6f5022d15ac8f293cee38358c.png[/img]
[h2]Pathfinding[/h2]

But visuals weren’t the only challenge.
The pathfinding system wasn’t exactly *thrilled* about verticality. The higher you went in the scene — and remember, these underground expeditions are technically floating far above the normal world — the more unstable and slow pathfinding became.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/be60557bb47e0482f5d1839f5be1b2088e1b9d5e.png[/img]

It added heavy strain on performance, especially compared to rendering, which handled the complex environments surprisingly well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1053429d21f6ebf6f5022d15ac8f293cee38358c.png[/img]
[h2]Modular design for a seamless flow![/h2]

These underground zones also rely on a layered level-loading system.

When you change levels in an underground building for example, the game unloads all other layers and then adds back the relevant ones based on your tracked position, starting from the bottom, and stopping at the level where you, as a player, are at this point in time.

This means the game is constantly checking where you are and only loading what’s relevant, which keeps performance smooth; even in a multi-level underground facility.

Another good example of the challenges verticality brought is the elevator shaft. It is very deep and not easy to navigate.
To improve the experience, the team tied the camera to the explorer on the vertical axis to have a smooth transition while going up and down, and worked hard to bring an immersive experience and manage light sources so they wouldn’t float or behave unnaturally when those walls disappear from view.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/74c46acb741d1140c90f0a6051786ad4a683a96a.png[/img]

Lighting, here again, was a tricky one. Since the game engine automatically hides the back sides of walls, any light that was placed on them would just… hover in mid-air. So instead, the team had to anchor lights to structural elements like pillars, to keep everything grounded.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1053429d21f6ebf6f5022d15ac8f293cee38358c.png[/img]
[h2]Wanna see a teleportation trick?[/h2]

One of the coolest technical tricks? You can walk in and out of the underground bunker with no loading screen, no button press — nothing.

How, you might ask?
Well, there’s a teleportation trigger placed at just the right spot at the elevator’s entrance/exit. The moment you walk into it, the game teleports you from the floating expedition level back to the surface base, and vice versa, all without breaking immersion.

This is the only place in the game where the player is teleported without any direct interaction.

[i]“We had to be extra careful,”[/i] the devs noted.
[i]“If you mess it up and the teleport loops, you could end up in a bugged-out limbo of infinite warping… and crash everything.”[/i]

So yeah… no pressure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1053429d21f6ebf6f5022d15ac8f293cee38358c.png[/img]

[b]TLDR;[/b] a *LOT* of experimentation and work went into building and getting the [i]“underground feeling”[/i] right. The team had to work around these issues while preserving that feeling of seamless descent into a tense, unknown place. A lot of tricks were pulled to keep everything stable, immersive, and believable!

We hope this peek behind the curtain shows just how much care went into crafting these expeditions.

See you ithere, Survivors!

notes.title: Behind-the-scenes of Expeditions in Endzone 2 - Part 1
notes.content:
Hello and good day Survivors!

You’ve noticed it: expeditions are back! And they have evolved.
In Endzone 2, expeditions are no longer isolated text-based events; they’re immersive, dynamic, and tied deeply into the world you explore. We sat down with the developers to share how this beloved feature has grown, what changed behind the scenes, and how your feedback is helping to shape what comes next!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1053429d21f6ebf6f5022d15ac8f293cee38358c.png[/img]
[h2]From walls of text to fully interactive expeditions[/h2]

In Endzone: A World Apart, expeditions were mostly about picking your specialists, gathering resources, and waiting to see what happened. And sometimes you had to wait… a lot! So essentially, expeditions were impactful, but not very interactive.

[b]BEFORE // Here’s a little trip down memory lane: one of those classic Endzone 1 expeditions in all its text-heavy glory…[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/b69aae29c55e4f098028091c17fbaf0ba120dd1a.png[/img]

In Endzone 2, expeditions are part of the gameplay loop, they are properly integrated into it. You stumble upon locations rather than initiating a big, separate mission. The experience is seamless, immersive, and engaging, with [b]mouse interaction, puzzles[/b], and [b]voiceovers[/b] adding depth to every expedition. More *actual gameplay*, less walls of text.

[b]AFTER // Look at this beaut'![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/bb87bd6a588c87f5270d817c8b8fd40ce304b11c.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1053429d21f6ebf6f5022d15ac8f293cee38358c.png[/img]
[h2]How Expeditions changed under the hood[/h2]

Reworking expeditions wasn’t just about adding polish, it also meant [b]creating, rebuilding[/b] or [b]improving[/b] core systems:
[list]
[*] [b]Lots of interactables![/b] Which now all need a name and a component to function. Everything you click and interact with has been carefully developed and integrated.
[*] [b]Inventory[/b] systems evolved! You can now bring items between locations and even prepare your own gear, like ladders, based on what you’ll need ahead.
[*] [b]Cameras[/b] adapt to complex environments, like underground buildings and elevator shafts.
[*] [b]Lighting, textures and shadows[/b] are hand-tuned to create the right atmosphere, especially underground.
[*] [b]Pathfinding[/b] for expeditions is a real challenge, and we’ve been actively working on improving it and making it smoother.
[*] [b]NPC interaction[/b] is also one of the most recent additions to expeditions. You’ll meet survivors you can talk to and interact with, and developers are interested in possibly expanding it.[/list]
And just to give you an idea…this [b]right here[/b]? 
This is just a [b]glimpse[/b] of the massive spaghetti tower of logic holding the expedition system together. 
[b]Please send snacks to the devs![/b] 🍕🍦🍩

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/a47494adc1da6bbdcd97d332e70193074d9c4ef7.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1053429d21f6ebf6f5022d15ac8f293cee38358c.png[/img]
[h2]Packing for the trip: a new Expedition inventory[/h2]

One of the biggest overhauls from Endzone 1 to Endzone 2? The [b]Expedition inventory system[/b].

Originally, every expedition had its [b]own isolated inventory[/b]. The items you found or needed were specific to that one expedition, which made sense, but also limited flexibility. Now, that’s changed entirely!

Expeditions in Endzone 2 use a [b]shared resource-based system[/b], where items come with different background colors to indicate their type, and most importantly: you can take them with you from one location to the next.

This means you might need to bring your own ladder, your own tools, or the right supplies! Because what you bring (or forget) directly affects what you can explore or unlock. You can also choose [b]different vehicles[/b], each with [b]varying cargo slots[/b], which opens up a whole layer of strategic prep before you even leave your settlement.

[quote] > Want to take more gear? Bring the van.
> Want to travel light and explore? Pack smart and take the buggy. [/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/47b815e5a6e75f855a2c6ff368e65cf6ba80231b.png[/img]

This shift has opened the door for more complex, layered expeditions, and the team already has extra items tucked in their back pocket, waiting to add even more realism and richness to your next outing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1053429d21f6ebf6f5022d15ac8f293cee38358c.png[/img]
[h2]Help us shape the future of Expeditions![/h2]

The future of Expeditions, like much of Endzone 2, is also shaped by you. And our devs are [b]*very*[/b] interested in hearing your thoughts on the forums, Discord, or here in the comments.

So here are a few questions from our very own devs, to *YOU*, Survivor:
[list][*] We heard some of you ask for "more complex expeditions", for example, what would that mean to you? 
[*]Would you like to see harder puzzles, or puzzles that are more creative, or spread out, encouraging deeper exploration?
[*]Would you like expeditions to feature bigger areas, more layered interactions, or simply more things to do?
[*]What kind of atmosphere are you looking for or expecting from expeditions? 
[*]Should they feel eerie, tense, dangerous? Would you like negative consequences if you make a wrong choice?
[*]The team is also very curious about your personal highlights:
[*]What are your top 3 favorite moments in an expedition so far?
[*]What do you look forward to experiencing again when heading out on an expedition?
[*]Every bit of feedback helps the team a ton, so we can work on building better expeditions that capture the right feeling in this post-apocalyptic world.[/list]
Answer here in the comments, in our Steam forums on in our [url=https://discord.gg/wupEznXjDD]Discord right here[/url]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1053429d21f6ebf6f5022d15ac8f293cee38358c.png[/img]
[h1]Up next in Part 2...[/h1]

Underground expeditions, how we worked on lighting & pathfinding, teleportation tricks, modular systems, and more! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/433a63e3885dffe5fecc005b20ac08c1638a3c01.png[/img]
Part 2 will dive deeper into the technical and visual challenges behind the game’s expedition system!

[i][b]Part 2 coming soon.[/b][/i]

notes.title: #9 Regular Update | Improvements, Bugfixes & More
notes.content:
Survivors,

This update delivers [b]different quality-of-life improvements[/b] and [b]long-requested UI upgrades[/b] to make your time in Endzone 2 smoother than ever. One highlight is the [b]"transfer all" button for looting ruins[/b] that has finally made it into the game.

We’ve also made a [b]key change to controls[/b]: the [b]number keys (1–0)[/b] are now dedicated to assigning and selecting vehicle groups, giving you [b]quicker access to your fleet[/b]. [b]Game speed controls[/b] have been moved to [b]new shortcuts[/b] to accommodate this change.

notes.title: Your thoughts on save game compatibility
notes.content:
[h3][b]An important message regarding full release[/b][/h3]

As we are approaching the full release of Endzone 2, which will take place later this year, there is one important thing we would like to share with you.

[h3][b]We are currently considering not making Early Access saves compatible with the full release version. Here's why:[/b][/h3]

From a developer's point of view, this gives us the opportunity to [b]get rid of some technical legacy issues[/b] that could cause problems in older save games due to the many updates. In addition, it helps us to [b]focus entirely on the game experience[/b] of a "fresh start" and thus not lose sight of the optimal gaming experience. The development effort is significantly reduced here.

From a player's perspective, we hope that you will be able to [b]enjoy Endzone 2 from a new beginning[/b] once again. It will be the first time that the [b]overall vision can be experienced[/b] in its entirety and only in a new game round can we ensure that you can [b]fully experience all the features with all its contents[/b].

We are [b]grateful for any feedback[/b] on this topic and hope that through this early communication we can [b]come to an alignment[/b] with you, the players, in the spirit of open development.

Feel free to jump into the discussion—whether it's in the [b]comments here[/b], on our [url=https://discord.com/channels/464772368280190976/1372885124135256107][b]Discord[/b][/url] or over on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2144640/discussions/0/612037567209084209/][b]Steam discussion board[/b][/url].

We're looking forward to a lively and productive discussion that leads to a result the majority can feel good about.

[b]Thank you![/b]

notes.title: #8 | Major Update | Dangers & Progression ☢️⚠️NOW LIVE
notes.content:
[b]Survivors,[/b]

We’ve just deployed our [b]biggest update[/b] yet for [b]Endzone 2[/b], and it’s going to challenge everything you know about [b]survival in the wasteland[/b]. From [b]radiation rework[/b] and brand-new buildings, to [b]deadly weather[/b] and [b]disease mechanics[/b] – the [b]Dangers & Progression[/b] update is live now!

This update also squashes bugs like [b]building placement issues[/b] and [b]expedition glitches[/b] for smoother play. Some tweaks make things even better, with stronger sandstorms, a refreshed disease system, and clearer radiation visuals. Updated tutorials make jumping in a breeze, pulling you deeper into this post-apocalyptic adventure!

[previewyoutube=oCRKG3McEGA;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Update Highlights Breakdown[/h2]

[h3][b]Major radiation system overhaul[/b][/h3]
→ Includes a detailed radiation overlay, cleansing rain, and irradiated food & water mechanics

[h3][b]New buildings[/b][/h3]
→ Decontaminator, Brewery, Bar, Coffee Shop, and more

[h3][b] New resources[/b][/h3]
→ Hops and Weed, used in beer and joint production

[h3][b]Upgraded storage buildings[/b][/h3]
→ Now remove radiation from food and water

[h3][b]4 new expeditions[/b][/h3]
→ Sewage Plant, Hospital, Traffic Accident, Small Ominous House

[h3][b] Game goal overhaul[/b][/h3]
→ New goal selection menu and 3 themed win conditions

[h3][b]Late-game content[/b][/h3]
→ Unlock Beacon monument and decorative statues through new missions

[h3][b]New missions & improved tutorials[/b][/h3]
→ Guides for new mechanics and content

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h2]☢️A New Era of Radiation☢️[/h2]
Radiation has evolved into a full survival mechanic. You’ll now need to:

[list]
[*] Monitor zone-based radiation with a new overlay
[*] Watch out for irradiated food and water
[*] Build Decontaminators and upgraded storage buildings to fight back
[*] Hope for cleansing rain – it now removes radiation naturally
[*] This rework adds new complexity, new visuals, and new threats.
[/list]

notes.title: [Sneak Peek] Major Update | Dangers & Progression Pt.2☢️⚠️
notes.content:
Hey Survivors!

Surviving the dangers of the wasteland is one thing. But what comes after survival? What keeps you going when your people are thriving, your cities are growing, and the sandstorms finally pass?

In today’s sneak peek, we’ll take a closer look at the "Progression" half of our upcoming [b]Dangers & Progression[/b] update — giving you new ways to shape your journey, define your victories, and push your settlements to the next level.

Let’s take a look...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/48a471424db814d4054ce43ff7e628df6c353a10.png[/img]

Whether you're aiming to grow a vast population, endure the harsh seasons, or build a thriving network of settlements—our new progression system gives your survival journey purpose, challenge, and a clear path to victory (or glorious defeat).

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Game Goals – A New Way to Play[/b][/u][/h3]

Every new game now begins with a choice: Do you play just for fun or do you pursue a greater purpose?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/587f89736f3ac2ed156f2d4a381427880f94b2ac.png[/img]

You can now select one of three Game Goals to define your play session:

[list][*] [b]Population Boom[/b] – Reach a total of 1000 adult settlers
[*] [b]Long-Term Survival[/b] – Endure 200 seasons
[*] [b]Expansionist[/b] – Create a total of 9 settlements[/list]
Completing a goal [b]earns you a shiny new achievement[/b] and the opportunity to [b]conclude[/b] the session. But don’t worry — you can always keep playing if your story isn’t finished yet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/26e075bae67eb8551e1477804e1b08086a0946ce.png[/img]

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: New Buildings – Function Meets Flavor[/b][/u][/h3]

To complement the new progression system, we’re introducing exciting [b]new buildings[/b] to [b]Endzone 2[/b]:

🏠 [b]Shelter[/b] – A compact housing solution for lots of adults, but no children. Ideal for dense late-game settlements.

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/5aba3c0b50eaf73ae89e0bef75410eeaf4a364e6.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/d237a1124d4c41ce3037a0630832a16812310e3f.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
☢️ [b]Decontaminator[/b] – Clears ground radiation in a moveable working area using up protective clothing. Essential for securing clean construction zones and protecting your settlers long-term.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/543c2cdcb637aa358a7cb48e352a9835e4c7e155.png[/img]

🍺 [b]Brewery & Pub[/b] – Grow hops, brew beer, and serve it in bars. Increases confidence for nearby housing, at the cost of a little health.

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/81e450bf596422c91d5602ce99cf041244deb2df.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/a62264d18959442e4dd9fd0d0a3115504cca4126.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/46be124ad3a9c663705834e850010b3b118271ed.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
🌿 [b]Coffee Shop[/b] – Cultivate weed, roll it into joints, and boost your settlers’ confidence. Just like the bar, it comes with a minor health penalty. Your people may be glowing with joy — but maybe also a little too chill.

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/07eed30b498de5e6c3ec492c4f1d7b912ece6d35.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/ab5c4f3b8c6f1d9f9233500f877cad48581a2daa.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
📡 [b]Beacon[/b] – Once your session goal is completed, you’ll unlock the ability to build the beacon. Construct it, and your people may leave this forsaken place for good… or stay behind to write a new future.

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/3c390fe030b4afdedf8785cf83715bdf58a26ad6.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/ff1cec394920e3b8b08fdd686baf46508e35e629.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/42f9db6da070a7dc60b8e3a5a45ba512219f74ea.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Monumental Progress[/b][/u][/h3]

We’ve also added 3 new late-game side missions with unique, challenging objectives. Completing them will reward you with special Monument Buildings:

[list][*] Each monument [b]boosts a specific stat[/b] for the settlement it’s placed in.
[*] But choose wisely; each one can [b]only be built once[/b]![/list]
These monuments not only give powerful bonuses but also stand as lasting reminders of your leadership and your people’s resilience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/38fd77cdd1dd809c2f7880fd1890ab9bf7906bd9.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

We hope you enjoyed this glimpse into the progression systems coming with the next major update. With new ways to win, build, and guide your people, this is one of our most exciting additions yet.

Thank you for all your support, feedback, and thoughts across every channel — we read everything, and your input helps shape the World of Endzone into something truly special.

Until next time, stay safe and don’t forget: every monument begins with a single settler. 🏗️ 💚

notes.title: [Sneak Peek] Major Update | Dangers & Progression Pt.1☢️⚠️
notes.content:
Hey survivors!

Hope your settlements are holding strong—because in our next major update, [b]Dangers & Progression[/b], we’re dialing things up a notch! While there’s plenty to talk about (yes, custom victory goals are coming!), today we want to give you a [b]first glimpse[/b] at something that’s been simmering beneath the surface: [b]the overhaul of environmental dangers[/b].

Let’s take a look at what’s coming soon...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/a77b4f432ae561ef245fbbef207adacca70ea038.png[/img]

From [b]reworked radiation zones[/b] to [b]deadlier sandstorms[/b] and [b]disease outbreaks[/b] that’ll really put your survival strategies to the test, the wasteland is becoming even [b]more unforgiving[/b]—and we couldn’t be more excited.

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Radiation Rework – A Deeper Threat Beneath Your Feet[/b][/u][/h3]

[b]Radiation [/b]is no longer just a simple value tied to each zone. Instead, it now [b]directly affects[/b] the ground itself. [b]Contaminated rain[/b] will irradiate the soil, while [b]clean rain[/b] helps decontaminate it over time.

A [b]brand-new overlay[/b] lets you view [b]ground radiation levels[/b], adding a strategic layer to building placement. [b]Constructing buildings on contaminated ground[/b] will raise your settlement’s overall radiation level—exposing your settlers to danger unless they’re equipped with [b]protective clothing[/b].

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/d4e7f9b991d2eb9821876cdbf3be9d47130c7c22.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/b104b8deed51493dd57f0dad0491e8e29e98f9c9.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Resources gathered from irradiated ground—like [b]food [/b]and [b]water[/b]—can now [b]contaminate [/b]a zone’s storage, [b]spreading the risk [/b]even further.

This system brings back some [b]familiar mechanics from Endzone 1[/b], requiring players to [b]think carefully[/b] about where they build and how they manage radiation to [b]keep their people safe[/b].

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/5ffcbea62cf3d47d285042e2844cd2ef9b828eb7.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/5ca16810c9f9ebc51146e6bc72a4f666eca59966.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Sandstorm Rework – No Longer Just Dust in the Wind[/b][/u][/h3]

The old "[i]Sanded[/i]" zone state is gone for good. Sandstorms now [b]pack a real punch[/b]—each time one strikes, some of your [b]buildings will take damage[/b].

If a building becomes [b]fully damaged[/b], it’ll [b]stop functioning[/b] until it’s repaired. Just like construction, repairs are handled by your [b]unemployed settlers[/b] and will require [b]resources to complete[/b].

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/33a95c022586c389e37eda181f60adc55d9decb6.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/84975ec9a03afd7ec77f74009bb4c41298c7ba33.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
To help you stay in control, you can now [b]disable all repairs[/b] in any given zone if needed—perfect for when [b]resources are tight[/b] or [b]priorities shift[/b].

This [b]new system[/b] turns sandstorms into a dynamic, ongoing threat that [b]forces tough decisions[/b] about what to fix, when, and where.

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/82d210ba3c8980ec5fbf45fd792821b248601123.png[/img][/th]
        [th]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/2675af4c72a0208cd0b7298f7bb36cbd60ad26f7.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Diseases[/b][/u][/h3]

The old "[i]Sick[/i]" zone state has been [b]removed[/b]. Now, when a [b]disease outbreak[/b] occurs, it [b]directly affects[/b] your settlers—several are randomly selected and become sick.

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7d329e7a0f1669b1fbe827a2a04b4d420d41769c.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/415e1ba167478f38473baf7bc0db808a8e8bcbc4.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Sick settlers are [b]unable to work[/b] and will stay that way [b]until they recover[/b]. Recovery can happen [b]naturally over time[/b] or be sped up by [b]visiting a hospital[/b]—just one of the new buildings from the upcoming update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/551186c21d25ead3fd5f8ae08a3cd45ec9626c27.png[/img]
This rework puts the [b]focus on individual well-being[/b] rather than a broad zone effect, making disease a [b]more personal[/b] and [b]impactful challenge[/b] to manage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

That’s all for now—but it’s only the beginning. We’ll be sharing more details soon about the second major part of this update: [b]Progression[/b]. You’ll be able to [b]define your own goals[/b] for each play session, giving you even [b]more control[/b] over how you survive and thrive in the wasteland. 

And that’s not all! Also part of the Progression topic, the update will bring [b]new buildings[/b], [b]fresh expeditions[/b], and [b]plenty of other additions[/b] to explore.

As always, a [b]huge thank you[/b] for your continued [b]support[/b], [b]feedback[/b], and [b]encouragement [/b]across Steam, Discord, and beyond. You’re helping shape the future of [b]Endzone 2[/b], and we can’t wait to show you what’s next. 💚

[i][b]Your Teams from Gentlymad & Assemble[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3]We’d love to have you join us on [url=https://discord.com/invite/worldofendzone]Discord[/url]! It’s the perfect place to share your feedback, connect with other players, and engage in discussions with our team.

[url=https://discord.com/invite/worldofendzone]Discord[/url] is our primary platform, and your input would be incredibly valuable. Don’t hesitate—come say hello! 😊[/h3]

notes.title: #6 | Major Update | Education & Bulletin Board 🎒📋 NOW LIVE
notes.content:
Survivors,

A new wave of improvements has arrived! This update introduces [b]Education[/b], featuring [b]Schools[/b], [b]Paper Mills[/b], and a system where settlers [b]earn Badges[/b] that [b]grant buffs[/b] to [b]settlement buildings[/b] and [b]expeditions[/b]. Children now grow into the next generation, and the [b]Bulletin Board[/b] helps settlers [b]notify you of new missions[/b]. Expeditions expand with the [b]new Endzone and Airfield sites[/b], while [b]Modding [/b]gets a [b]soft launch[/b] for early experimentation.

We've also added [b]Upcycling improvements[/b], including [b]new ruins[/b] like the [b]Park[/b], [b]Hospital[/b], and[b] Fish Farm[/b], plus [b]"Find Trader"[/b] missions. Settlers now have [b]improved life cycles and visuals[/b], making your world feel more alive.

Finally, [b]numerous fixes[/b] and [b]tweaks enhance the UI[/b], [b]pathfinding[/b], [b]missions[/b], and [b]expeditions[/b], alongside [b]balancing updates[/b] for [b]radiation[/b], [b]trade[/b], and [b]resources[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

Last but not least this update also includes our [b]first iteration of Modding support[/b]!

Modding was a [b]highly requested feature[/b], and it was on our list from the [b]very beginning of Endzone 2’s development[/b]. Now, we’re thrilled to introduce the [b]very first moddable version[/b] of the game! [b]It’s still in its early stages[/b], but already allows you to [b]mod several textures, sprites, audio files, and even add your own localizations[/b].

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]

        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/c849c2259ef00434d34f2be7a0fdc74bfd59dd22.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
We chose [b]mod.io[/b] as our platform to handle mods, as it gives us the ability to also enable [b]modding for the whole player base across multiple platforms[/b].

[b]Disclaimer:[/b] [i]Please be aware that modding capabilities are still very limited but we want to put this out early to get early feedback and harden the infrastructure. [/i]

To help you get started, we’ve put together a [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3430275798]comprehensive Modding Guide[/url]. Happy modding!

notes.title: [Sneak Peek] Major Update | Education & Bulletin Board 🎒📋
notes.content:
Survivors!

The release of our next major update, [b]Education & Bulletin Board[/b], is fast approaching! To get you excited, we’re offering a [b]sneak peek[/b] at what’s coming your way. So, without further ado—let’s dive in!

Just like in our previous sneak peek, here’s some [b]basic information[/b] about the [b]main features[/b] of this update:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/4d1728b77b18bddf689de56915fdd581a34b552a.png[/img]

With this update and the newly introduced overall theme [b]Education[/b], you can shape your settlements' future early on. Because [b]Education is key[/b]!

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Schools[/b][/u][/h3]

Schools are the heart of learning, [b]employing dedicated teachers[/b] who help pave the path forward. As long as a teacher is present, children can attend—and when they [b]grow up[/b], they receive a [b]Badge[/b], marking their journey into the next stage of life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/919ca02d185aabcee9539709e41fc2e494b631c9.png[/img]
The type of [b]Badge [/b]a child earns is influenced by [b]you, the player[/b]. Each Zone offers a[b] variety of available Badges[/b], and you decide which ones are allowed. When a child grows up, they have an equal chance of receiving any permitted Badge. For example, if three Badges are available, each has a [b]⅓ probability of being awarded[/b]. However, a child can only ever receive one Badge—making your choices even more impactful.

There are [b]several Badges[/b], each providing [b]unique bonuses and drawbacks[/b] that influence different aspects of the game. Every Settler with a Badge [b]contributes a portion of its effect[/b] to the entire zone, subtly [b]shaping its dynamics[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1a94b20b2a180a8a16d332100fb4d0349c95638e.png[/img]
Every school has a [b]set number[/b] of student slots. If more children are present in a Zone than the school can accommodate, [b]not all of them[/b] will receive a Badge when they grow up. Managing space wisely ensures [b]the best possible future[/b] for your young citizens!

A thriving school also needs resources. Therefore, [b]schools consume paper[/b] while operating, so keeping your supply stocked [b]ensures smooth learning[/b].

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Papermill[/b][/u][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/27905cdd491e956be61c0777d87b552c71f6f70e.png[/img]
[b]Paper[/b]—how do we get it? Glad you asked! Paper can be produced in the [b]Papermill[/b], a [b]new building[/b] introduced in this update. The [b]Papermill [/b]creates paper using water and reed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/c451fc5d8993df8bd7ea3b8b46d7520b984137fb.png[/img]
Introducing [b]Reed[/b]—a versatile new crop for your [b]Swamp Farm[/b]! Hardy and resilient, this resource [b]thrives in wetland conditions[/b], offering [b]new opportunities for crafting and production[/b]. Keep your farms flourishing and make the most of this [b]valuable addition[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/8dbd01652536a20861e93afe53a9c8791b84278e.png[/img]

The introduction of [b]Bulletin Boards[/b] gives your settlers a voice—and you the opportunity to listen. At the Bulletin Board, you'll receive settlers' requests that can boost their contentment, as well as quests that help improve your settlement. Completing these tasks may reward you with additional resources and other valuable benefits. The Bulletin Board can be [b]found[/b] at your [b]Town Center[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/ca3e5f4682e1555f76a514ed8e60ea3cdd94c817.png[/img]
A variety of [b]events and quests[/b] are tied to the Bulletin Board, unfolding throughout your session. Be sure to [b]check the board regularly[/b], or your settlers' overall [b]contentedness may decline[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/8a4890ddc5efed909de8e584c7280d709cb9debc.png[/img]
[b]On a side note[/b]: You’ll now receive [b]fewer direct event dialogues[/b], as many of these events will be [b]redirected to the Bulletin Board[/b] for you to review at your convenience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

Besides these two big topics, [b]the update[/b] will bring [b]a lot more to the game[/b] which we will cover in the update's [b]comprehensive changelog next week[/b]. 🔥

Until then, feel free to share your [b]thoughts[/b], [b]feedback[/b], and [b]ideas[/b]—particularly about the [b]features mentioned[/b] in this posting. 

Thank you for your ongoing support. Talk soon!

notes.title: Dev Q&A—You asked, we answered! [Part 2]
notes.content:
[h3]Hello, Survivors from all horizons![/h3]

We're back with Part 2 of our Q&A, where we continue answering your questions about Endzone 2.
Last week, we covered six questions—this time, we're tackling the last five, sent by you on Discord and Steam.

[b]We will have quite a lot of screenshots to show you in the first answer about the Visual Design Process, we thus uploaded them to [url=https://imgur.com/a/endzone-2-visual-design-process-OWUFTID]Imgur here[/url] and they are also individually linked below so you can go and check them in their full size without encumbering this blogpost :)[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/ca34776878a9a20cbd67ad9d0c4672f35b4f999c.png[/img]

Let's jump straight into it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[i][Visual Design Process][/i]
[h3]Q1: Which parts of the process did you find most enjoyable and challenging while bringing these environments to life?[/h3]
[b][list][*]For example, things like creating textures for the landscape or modeling certain buildings come to mind, but I’d love to hear which parts stood out to you the most in terms of enjoyment and challenges.[/list][/b][i]From: ShadZ[/i]
_

[b]A: [/b]The visual development process begins with an ideation phase, where concept artists generate a broad spectrum of ideas. These range from loose, exploratory concepts—such as setting the overall mood and tone of expeditions, vehicle designs, and city structures—to more refined and specific design elements, like mock-ups of zones in various states or detailed depictions of settlers. Here are some examples:The visual development process begins with an ideation phase, where concept artists generate a broad spectrum of ideas. These range from loose, exploratory concepts—such as setting the overall mood and tone of expeditions, vehicle designs, and city structures—to more refined and specific design elements, like mock-ups of zones in various states or detailed depictions of settlers. Here are some examples:

[url=https://imgur.com/roNQS6p]Ideation phase (1)[/url]
[url=https://imgur.com/mJJEaFw]Ideation phase (2)[/url]
[url=https://imgur.com/wmMOWGg]Ideation phase (3)[/url]

The most promising outcomes of this phase are formalized in the Style Guide or Art Bible. The Style Guide captures the project's overall visual essence and design direction. Influenced by game design and the team's creative vision, it serves as both a starting point and a reference for internal team members as well as external stakeholders, including publishers and contractors. E.g.: 

[url=https://imgur.com/Win8ctG]Style Guide / Art Bible examples (1)[/url]
[url=https://imgur.com/nl9cHfO]Style Guide / Art Bible examples (2)[/url]
[url=https://imgur.com/7SJblS3]Style Guide / Art Bible examples (3)[/url]
[url=https://imgur.com/J0GcAyA]Style Guide / Art Bible examples (4)[/url]
[url=https://imgur.com/etGs4Cj]Style Guide / Art Bible examples (5)[/url]
[url=https://imgur.com/zCH81s1]Style Guide / Art Bible examples (6)[/url]

In addition to the Style Guide, we maintained a Building Design Breakdown in our project wiki. This resource provided a structured and analytical approach to building design, with practical guidelines focusing on key elements such as footprint, form, color, and materials. It aimed to support artists throughout multiple stages of development.

[url=https://imgur.com/qE7b37m]Building Design Breakdown (1)[/url]
[url=https://imgur.com/AdfBlP5]Building Design Breakdown (2)[/url]
[url=https://imgur.com/HpG9Tm9]Building Design Breakdown (3)[/url]
[url=https://imgur.com/bImyo90]Building Design Breakdown (4)[/url]
[url=https://imgur.com/rcFsqQP]Building Design Breakdown (5)[/url]

One of the primary challenges during the art and design process was balancing creative goals with economic and technical constraints. Economic factors such as time, budget, team size, and skill level played a critical role, alongside technical considerations related to the chosen engine, tools, and development framework.
Personally, the early concepting stage was the most exciting part of the project. It allowed us the freedom to explore design ideas and visual themes without limitations.
I’m incredibly proud of the art team and what we achieved in a short time frame. The sheer amount of creative content that made it into the final game, although it is not perfect, is a testament to their talent and dedication.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[i][Revisiting History?][/i]
[h3]Q2: A lot of the buildings and even processes actually create a bad footprint similar to that which destroyed the place - how can this game be played so that I don't have to have ugly power stations and destructive mining.[/h3]
[i]From: LaurieBrooker[/i]
_

[b]A: [/b]Endzone 2 offers various options that depend on the style of play.

On the one hand, the new mechanic of being able to create multiple settlements comes into play here. If a player wants to build a settlement in harmony with nature, he can relocate industrial buildings to other zones and deliver their resources via transport routes.

If every settlement is to be built as nature-friendly as possible, you can try to find and produce as many of the resources whose production would harm the environment as possible in Badlands or buy them from traders.

In addition to some industrial buildings, settlements in Endzone 2 are already designed with sustainability in mind. For example, we have deliberately avoided using coal or gas power plants to generate electricity because we believe that humanity would not make this mistake again.

[url=https://imgur.com/X7ufxh1]Screenshot here![/url]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[i][Inspirations][/i]
[h3]Q3: What are you main inspirations for your work? Where do you go to get ideas for your setting and where do you look to in game design?[/h3][i]From: Winona[/i]
_

[b]A: [/b]The world of Endzone has always been influenced by common post-apocalypse series and games. However, we have always emphasized a more realistic approach that incorporates current issues such as climate change rather than going down the Mad Max road. 🙂 So while series such as Chernobyl were a model for the atmosphere in a nuclear catastrophe, we also drew on daily knowledge and discussions about climate change. In particular, documentary thought experiments on how to survive in a world shaken by climate change were very insightful. You can learn a lot about this on YouTube...

When it comes to game design, we naturally take our own ideas in the first place. But we had to lie if we didn't keep an eye on current city builders, both genre giants and indie developers alike. Play a lot, learn a lot. In the end, however, we always try to add our own touch to the game design.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[i][Modding][/i]
[h3]Q4: Do you have a checklist for stuff you want to include in modding?[/h3][b][list][*]Are you going to provide us with tools and what not or a series of guides?[/list][/b][i]From: Bum[/i]
_

[b]A: [/b]Currently, we are planning a soft launch of our modding capabilities. So first we want to ship the basic infrastructure, giving the option to mod minor things (icons, loca, etc.). If this goes well and we could gather some feedback about the process we want to keep extending it (allowing you to add new buildings e.g.). Along with every release we also want to ship guides on how to actually do modding.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3]Q5: Is there a time frame on your calendar where you will drop back and fix some of the problems that a user/player with an OLDer GPU (ie 4 years) card may be unable to start the game at all?[/h3]
[i]From: oldman_dr[/i]
_

[b]A: [/b]Thank you for contributing your question. We recently switched to DirectX 11 being our default rendering technique to better the situation and we are also working on more improvements in an upcoming release. This won't help out with all graphics cards however, since we do require certain feature levels to make the game work, since some of the game logic runs on GPU instructions. So iGPUs and GPUs under feature Level 12_0 (DirectX 11.3) still won't be able to run the game.

Sadly, hardware manufacturers didn't make it easy to get clear intel on what hardware is installed and what the capabilities are, as you can see it in this table, everything is quite fragmented and not easily distinguishable (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feature_levels_in_Direct3D)


This was the latest hotfix regarding DirectX 11: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2144640/view/512947503265480794

notes.title: Dev Q&A—You asked, we answered! [Part 1]
notes.content:
[h3]Good day Survivors![/h3]

We gathered your questions about Endzone 2 from Discord and Steam in the context of this Q&A, and now it's time to share the answers.

Today, we’re diving into [b]Part 1[/b] of our Q&A, with [b]Part 2[/b] coming next Thursday.
In this [b]Part 1[/b], we will be answering 6 questions, while [b]Part 2[/b] will contain 5.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/ca34776878a9a20cbd67ad9d0c4672f35b4f999c.png[/img]

No more waiting—let’s get straight to the answers!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3]Q1: The Elephant in the Room: Appeasing the Mixed Reviewers?[/h3]
[b][list][*]What are some of the ideas the devs are all considering to appease or at a minimum, regain player interest enough to offset the mixed reviews that results in new positive ones?[/list][/b][i]From: c0mad0r[/i]
_

[b]A: [/b]Of course, we noticed the mixed reviews and gave it a lot of thought. First and foremost, we initially have disappointed many EZ1 veterans with our new approach, that cannot be dismissed.

So since our first playtest, we have tried to get closer to EZ1 again. For example, we have worked significantly on the diversity of our settler simulation and have incorporated various ideas from our players based on their feedback to close the gap between EZ1 and EZ2. The latter includes, for example, visual improvements to our buildings as well as removing new mechanics that didn't make any sense, like our settlement branches.

We also plan to bring back familiar mechanics that will be reminiscent of EZ1, but will also be reinterpreted within the capabilities of EZ2. This includes, for example, the topic of radiation, which we want to revise in Early Access.

At the core, however, we are trying to stay true to our original vision and hope that with the pending updates we can convince our players at last! 🙂

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3]Q2: If everything goes according to plan, what would you like to introduce in Endzone 2 until the end of 2025?[/h3]
[i]From: StarlordDrax[/i]
_

[b]A: [/b]What we have communicated so far is an Early Access period of 1 year. This means that we plan to leave Early Access in mid-2025. 

Until then we will release the [b]Education/Bulletin Board Update[/b], as well as [b]2 other major updates[/b]. One of the last two major updates will probably deal with a revision of the radiation system as well as further challenges and the other will probably bring raiders back into the game. Still, these two updates are always subject to change! 

In between, we will continue with our regular updates, which are intended to further improve the game, especially in terms of usability and stability. What comes after we leave Early Access depends heavily on the success of the full release and the feedback from our players. 😌 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3]Q3: How far ahead are the content updates planned into the Roadmaps?[/h3]
[b][list][*]Do you have the pair of patches (fixes+content) all planned out for the whole of Early Access? Or is it fluid depending on what bubbles up from majority sentiment?
[*]If there are major pain points or wishlisted features that players bring up, is that woven into the roadmap or things are gonna get reshuffled?[/list][/b][i]From: ellacharmed[/i]
_

[b]A: [/b]Of course, we have our own vision of where the journey should go, not least because of the predecessor Endzone - A world apart. 
However, we constantly try to compare our ideas with player feedback and are happy to respond to new opportunities that arise as a result. Fortunately, the feedback often coincides with our own vision. Another reason for our flexible approach to player feedback is that Endzone 2 is fundamentally different from its predecessor. Early Access is therefore also an important tool for understanding whether we are on the right path. And as we all know this has already paid off... 🙂

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3]Q4: What development strategy will you choose for the game after its release?[/h3]
[list][*][b]Will you work on Endzone 2 for many years, constantly releasing various patches and DLCs, or will you develop Endzone 3?[/b][/list][i]From: }{руm[/i]
_

[b]A: [/b]We are currently focusing entirely on the Early Access. 
What will happen after depends heavily on the success of the full release, but of course we would like to continue developing Endzone 2 for as long as possible. 
Looking at the current numbers, we are behind our expectations, but we are doing our best to make the game a success.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3]Q5: In Endzone1 there was a DLC - Distant Places that was released. [...] 
Are you planning to introduce something similar in order to unlock unique buildings and recipes along with lore and lovely NPCs... and maybe crazy dangerous missions in more distant lands??[/h3]
[b][list][*]My other question is: What about other people that were saved (Endzone1)?? Are we going to meet other Factions?? Will Raiders come back to wreak havoc on us?[/list][/b][i]From: BloodFire[/i]
_

[b]A: [/b]We naturally draw on many ideas from Endzone 1 and its DLCs. Prosperity, in particular, was something we had in mind for Endzone 2 right from the start. The progress towards cement, glass and a technological advanced civilization in general can already be found in Endzone 2. However, we can't pursue all ideas from EZ1. Narrative areas outside of the usual map, such as in Distant Places, are not yet part of our plans, even though we loved the stories. Maybe we'll find other ways to tell exciting stories in the future.

Regarding raiders, we are very keen to bring them back to Endzone 2 during Early Access. Besides traders, which already exist in the game, these are the only two types of factions we currently have planned.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3]Q6: Name a couple of ideas that you would really like to implement, but there is no way to add them to the game.[/h3]
[i]From: }{руm[/i]

When it comes to what we want but will never be able to build in, that's a difficult question...

In Endzone 2 there will probably never be a first person mode in which you can move through your settlements. Grid-less construction will also not be possible in the foreseeable future.

But you have to keep some of your ambitions open for future projects anyway... 😉

notes.title: #5 Regular Update | Improvements, Bugfixes & More
notes.content:
Survivors!

Today, we released a [b]Regular Update[/b] packed with [b]new features[/b], [b]quality-of-life improvements[/b], and a [b]large number of fixes[/b]. 

This update introduces [b]new trading mechanics[/b], [b]enhanced electricity management[/b], and [b]UI refinements[/b] to improve your gameplay experience. [b]Traders missions[/b] can be completed [b]directly [/b]in the [b]trading post UI[/b] now, and [b]resource flow calculations[/b] have been [b]improved[/b]. [b]Electricity management[/b] sees [b]major upgrades[/b], including power poles that can now be [b]built on streets[/b] and [b]better visualization[/b] of the energy network. The [b]camera system[/b] has been [b]refined[/b], with [b]zooming via keyboard[/b] and smoother [b]fixed-camera movements[/b].

We’ve also addressed a [b]variety of bugs across expeditions[/b], [b]buildings[/b], [b]vehicles[/b], and [b]UI elements[/b], improving overall stability. [b]Tweaks [/b]to [b]settler behaviors[/b], [b]trade routes[/b], and [b]statistics [/b]ensure a smoother and more intuitive gameplay experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/2366561470be835a56cc4e8df467f98779495d78.gif[/img]
[list]
[*][b]Camera:[/b] Added subtle mouse-position-based camera movement for all fixed camera positions (e.g., main menu, trading posts, and expeditions).
[*][b]Camera:[/b] The camera can now be zoomed using the keyboard.
[*][b]Electricity:[/b] Power poles can now be built on streets.
[*][b]Traders:[/b] Resource per minute calculations now correctly account for goods transferred via trade routes.
[*][b]Traders:[/b] Trader missions can now be completed directly in the trading post UI.
[/list]

[*][b]Camera:[/b] Tooltips are no longer hidden when moving or rotating the camera with keyboard input.
[*][b]Electricity:[/b] Paused buildings are now correctly reflected in the electricity analytics view.
[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] All expeditions are now correctly sorted by sector in the expedition overview.
[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed expedition interaction dialog.
[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed glitchy floor blending in the sand mine.

[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed number riddle code 7599 not being readable in all cases (adjusted font and number positioning).
[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed road and vegetation being incorrectly highlighted in the starting endzone.
[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed an issue where the explorer could glitch through lootable boxes in the scrapyard.
[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed an issue where the explorer could glitch through the wheels of a buggy in the endzone POI.
[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed a seemingly unlooted barrel in the Wind Generator expedition.
[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed the 88% bug in the modern house expedition.
[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed trading posts incorrectly counting toward overall sector progress in the expedition overview.
[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed the sorting of expeditions in the overview to reflect the correct sector order.
[*][b]Input:[/b] Fixed a rare error that could occur when deselecting objects.
[*][b]Input:[/b] The current selection is now correctly cleared when starting to build roads.

[*][b]Traders:[/b] Traders now inform players when they have no available mission and will notify them when one becomes available.

[*][b]UI:[/b] Updated the "Access Points" help text image.
[*][b]UI:[/b] World overview (previously zone overview) now also includes all discovered traders.

[*][b]Vehicles:[/b] Improved performance when moving multiple selected vehicles to a new position.
[*][b]Vehicles:[/b] Interaction buttons in the vehicle inspector are now always visible to prevent UI jumping when the selected vehicle is moving.

notes.title: Hotfix | V 0.8.9146.30060 #3587869d7
notes.content:
Survivors!

today we release a small hotfix consisting of bugfixes and stability improvements.

[b][i]We’ve identified issues that could cause freezes and crashes when using Vulkan. As a result, we’ve optimized the DirectX 11 version to deliver comparable performance and improved stability. DirectX 11 is now the default launch option. If you’ve experienced freezes or crashes, please try running DirectX 11. Vulkan remains available but is currently considered unstable.[/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[*][b]Buildings:[/b] Fixed free workforce at worker amount slider displaying 0 when clicking on a production building for the first time in a game session.
[*][b]System:[/b] Fixed several potential memory leaks, especially when creating new sessions while a session was running.
[*][b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed Endzone expedition not being finishable.
[*][b]Camera:[/b] Fixed errors when the camera was following an entity that does not longer exist.

notes.title: Early Access 2024 Recap
notes.content:
Survivors!

We hope you’ve been enjoying some relaxing holidays so far! It’s been an overwhelming Early Access journey, and as we approach the turn of the year, we’d like to reflect on everything that’s happened since Endzone 2 entered Early Access in August.

[b]Before diving into the update recap, we want to extend a heartfelt thank you to you—our community and players. We wouldn’t be here without your incredible support and passion for the game. Your love and dedication are truly invaluable.

From all of us at Gentlymad Studios and Assemble Entertainment, thank you so much. Here’s to an amazing Early Access journey in 2025![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7f8196eb03fa8b49229b48a4712bc4cfceee085b.png[/img]

[h3]Let's start with the Regular and Major Updates that happened this year:[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7f8196eb03fa8b49229b48a4712bc4cfceee085b.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/379cc7610779b96fd27059019794b09354004ecf.png[/img]

The first [b]Regular Update[/b] in September brought you an extensive update to the[b] ingame statistic data[/b]. Also this was the first version of the statistics window which will be further improved in future updates. 

Additionally, you got the option to [b]rename settlers and vehicles[/b] for a more immersive gameplay experience. Besides these, [b]new expededitions[/b], [b]bug fixes[/b] and several [b]gameplay improvements[/b] were part of this update.

[list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/958e23d57b96d4e82590077b61678813c6c457c8.png[/img][/list]
[table noborder=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img] {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/5c43032ff0fbf467b59d90b93cda89415d5d0555.gif[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1a6e83bc405f1e651856d62be4d546a76148cfd8.gif[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7f8196eb03fa8b49229b48a4712bc4cfceee085b.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/507466e1ae334851414e722f49fa8ac7f087316f.png[/img]

This transformative update introduced powerful [b]new technologies[/b] to your settlements. Harness the energy of the elements with [b]Wind Turbines[/b], [b]Solar Power Systems[/b], and more as you connect buildings using [b]Power Poles[/b] and [b]Relay Stations[/b], igniting a new era of resource management and community growth.

On top, the update also introduced the [b]upcycling mechanic[/b] that lets you [b]make use of valuable ruins[/b], including [b]coal and copper mines[/b], reclaiming essential resources for your survival and jump start your efforts to restore human civilization.

[previewyoutube=1vSOsshX3Qg;full][/previewyoutube]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7f8196eb03fa8b49229b48a4712bc4cfceee085b.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/964a65fa7ee6700e4a999a15e87e00c8e4ce11e5.png[/img]

November's Regular Update included [b]Quality of Life features[/b], [b]bug fixes[/b], and [b]plenty of gameplay improvements[/b]—not to mention [b]additional content[/b], such as new expeditions.

In a nutshell, this update's focus was on providing you with [b]a better and more immersive game start[/b], several [b]new and complex expeditions[/b], as well as a [b]revamped radiation system[/b], making it easier to understand and less unforgiving.

[list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/5420025c56b176ea85fe1a3e90d20136cd8ad9ec.gif[/img][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7f8196eb03fa8b49229b48a4712bc4cfceee085b.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/319f75dda12cc9e229cc0b9de524ef1614f669e0.png[/img]

This update brought you exciting [b]new additions[/b] and [b]improvements [/b]to enhance your journey! 

[b]Traders [/b]now populate the world, offering [b]unique loot[/b], [b]reputation missions[/b], and an engaging [b]bargaining system[/b]. The intermediate area [b]connects zones with electricity[/b] using new [b]power poles[/b], a [b]construction vehicle[/b], and a [b]detailed electricity overview[/b]. 

We also added [b]animals [/b]to zones as well as the [b]Hunting Lodge[/b] as a new building, which allows your settlers to [b]actively hunt animals[/b] in their territory. Also, settlers now spend additional time in buildings and moving directly to construction sites, [b]enhancing productivity[/b] and the beloved [b]“Wuselfaktor”[/b].

[previewyoutube=0GZRrbrBfm4;full][/previewyoutube]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7f8196eb03fa8b49229b48a4712bc4cfceee085b.png[/img]

We hope you’re enjoying the current version of the game as much as we do! While a lot has already been added since Endzone 2 launched in Early Access this summer, there’s still a long road ahead—and so much more to add and improve based on both your feedback and (y)our vision for the game.

Stay tuned for exciting updates in 2025 as we continue to shape Endzone 2 together!

See you in 2025—Happy New Year, Survivors!

[i]Your Teams from Gentlymad & Assemble

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2144640/Endzone_2/

[h2]A hub for all things Endzone: Discord & Community News 🌱[/h2]

If you’re looking to stay updated and connect with other survivors, our Discord is the place to be! 
We have dedicated channels and roles designed to provide you with exactly the information you're looking for, whether it is patch notes, dev blogs, or community life updates.

You can take a second to join the Discord [url=https://discord.gg/worldofendzone]right here[/url] and tailor your experience to your needs and preferences!

Keeping track of everything happening in a game community can be a challenge, so we’ve specifically created a [b]Community News[/b] channel on Discord. Here, you’ll find updates on new community activities, fresh discussion topics, polls, weekly questions, milestone celebrations, and improvements to our Discord & community!

We've also added a dedicated [b]Streams and Media[/b] channel to showcase all the content you’re creating around Endzone. Whether it’s streams, videos, screenshots, or anything else creative, this is the place to share your work with other survivors and get noticed! 
You might even have your content featured on our social media!

We can't wait to see you with us in the [url=https://discord.gg/worldofendzone]Endzone[/url]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/2c49039606dd52d88d228ba014c52d2be86cf011.png[/img]

notes.title: [Sneak Peek] Major Update | Traders & Hunting 💸🏹
notes.content:
Survivors!

Before the Major update, called [b]Traders & Hunting[/b], is being released on [b]December 13th[/b] already, we'd like to give you a sneak peek at the content of this update, so here we go.

Just like in our previous sneak peek, here’s some basic information about the main features of this update:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/c68b3d528915aedfec3af7169fe405d2af81d9fc.png[/img]

Using your vehicles to navigate the badlands will eventually lead you to a [b]trader's shop[/b]. Be sure to pay them a visit and start trading by [b]exchanging goods[/b]. You'll be amazed by what they have to offer—they’re always worth the trip.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7ee7ebcb99d9f7ee0b6bed8e4bc25a87f00f99d8.png[/img]

The [b]Hunting Lodge[/b] is an additional building for [b]food production[/b]. As long as animals are present within its working radius, the Hunting Lodge will [b]continuously produce food[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Rusty's Shop[/b][/u][/h3]

Each trader has their own [b]unique Trading Post[/b] located somewhere in the badlands. The screenshot below showcases [b]Rusty's shop[/b], where you'll meet the feisty and good-humored trader [b]Rusty Rolph[/b], always ready with a snappy saying to brighten your day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/3ce971b46cc7ab95f2afc378e82580ac7424f14c.png[/img]
Bargaining with a trader can be tricky, so make sure to keep them satisfied with your offers. Otherwise, they might lose patience, and you'll [b]risk damaging your reputation[/b] with them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/a70d17f786def4892fff9b4c1c16f5428c7d652c.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Hunting Lodge[/b][/u][/h3]

As mentioned in the introduction, the [b]Hunting Lodge[/b] is a new building in [b]Endzone 2[/b] that supplies your settlement with food. What makes the [b]Hunting Lodge[/b] unique is that its production [b]remains consistent even during a drought[/b]—setting it apart from other food sources.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/86fac5fcaf01abed0fe6f143ad75aa9dfafdb852.png[/img]
[b]Wildlife will now spawn in zones[/b] to support food production. For now, there are two types of animals: [b]deer [/b]and [b]boars[/b]. However, be cautious not to overhunt them—they need time to recover and repopulate.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

While we’re putting the[b] final touches on the update[/b] to ensure it’s the best it can be, we’re also excited to[b] involve you more closely[/b] in our development process. To do this, we plan to utilize Steam’s newly enhanced [b]Beta Branch feature[/b], which has become much [b]more user-friendly[/b] for both developers and players.

We want to offer you—[b]the heart of our community[/b]—the opportunity to [b]test upcoming updates[/b] before they go live. Your feedback will be invaluable, helping us [b]improve gameplay[/b] and [b]catch any potential bugs[/b] before the official release. Best case scenario would be to have this ready ahead of the [b]Traders & Hunting[/b] update's release on [b]December 13[/b], though we appreciate your understanding if we need a little more time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

notes.title: #3 Regular Update | Improvements, Bugfixes & More
notes.content:
Survivors!

It's time for our bi-monthly [b]Regular Update[/b]! Today's update includes Quality of Life features, bug fixes, and plenty of gameplay improvements—not to mention additional content, such as new expeditions.

In a nutshell, we focused on providing you with a better and more immersive game start, several new and complex expeditions, as well as a revamped radiation system, making it easier to understand and less unforgiving.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]
[b]Before we get to the detailed changelog, here's an important note:[/b]
[list]
[*] Some voice overs are currently missing from the game as they are still pending re-recording.
[*] Lock picks will not have a usecase anymore in this version. This will potentially be addressed with the next update.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/2366561470be835a56cc4e8df467f98779495d78.gif[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]Missions:[/b] The start of the game now features a (skippable) cutscene that introduces the world and basic objectives in a more immersive way.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/5420025c56b176ea85fe1a3e90d20136cd8ad9ec.gif[/img]
[*] [b]Missions:[/b] The game now starts next to an Endzone.
[*] [b]Expeditions:[/b] Added new Endzone expedition.[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/effe54681379f2ec8b385a7a04cb8624d352d4d6.png[/img][list][*] [b]Expeditions:[/b] Added Military Base expedition with new riddle type.[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/bb2b18a74090d196874685f7c863d86fc9b139cd.png[/img][list][*] [b]UI:[/b] UI now tries to restore selections after another UI was displayed.
[*] [b]Menu:[/b] Added Endzone ruin set to the main menu.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/38c7b7e09d6369437e312fc029f0bd5e11468a28.gif[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]Buildings:[/b] Adjusted the layout of production progress to fit larger numbers.
[*] [b]Buildings:[/b] Fixed flickering upcycling ruins icons.
[*] [b]Buildings:[/b] Fixed field of influence resetting its center when the respective building is upgraded.
[*] [b]Buildings:[/b] Fixed label for paused construction site info.
[*] [b]Buildings:[/b] Fixed pharmacy not displaying buffs in the buff analytics view.
[*] [b]Buildings:[/b] Fixed the wrong UI being displayed for certain buildings.
[*] [b]Buildings:[/b] Paused construction sites no longer show missing builders notifications.
[*] [b]Buildings:[/b] World tasks can no longer be placed as blueprints since they don't have construction costs.
[*] [b]Camera:[/b] Fixed a bug related to animated cameras.
[*] [b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed total progress display for several nodes.
[*] [b]Expeditions:[/b] Loot to go ruins again show their inventories in the inspector.
[*] [b]Map:[/b] Fixed missing road sections for 1-anchor ruins.
[*] [b]Minimap:[/b] Fixed minimap pings not resetting correctly when switching between sessions.
[*] [b]Missions:[/b] Fixed bad coloring in the event overview and events in the HUD.
[*] [b]Missions:[/b] Fixed the wrong location being displayed in dialog when settling on a new zone.
[*] [b]Options:[/b] Fixed the UI not displaying the system keyboard layout display string for key bindings.
[*] [b]Research:[/b] Fixed errors caused by missing technologies.
[*] [b]Savegames:[/b] Fixed incorrect energy values in existing savegames.
[*] [b]Session:[/b] Fixed knowledge points being calculated incorrectly when unlocking bridges from the session options.
[*] [b]Settlers:[/b] Fixed a broken health tooltip.
[*] [b]Statistics:[/b] Fixed a case-sensitive comparison in the search field.
[*] [b]Statistics:[/b] Fixed the wrong RPM trend being displayed in statistics.
[*] [b]UI:[/b] Camera can no longer be moved while an overview UI is open.
[*] [b]UI:[/b] Cleaned up several icons.
[*] [b]UI:[/b] Efficiency tooltips no longer mention workforce as a factor for buildings without workforce.
[*] [b]UI:[/b] Fixed errors in the entity tooltip.
[*] [b]UI:[/b] Fixed logic for selecting multiple units using Ctrl.
[*] [b]UI:[/b] Fixed a pause info issue where the displayed button wouldn’t update if the key mapping was changed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/281a82ab4ce953a75b80e435c91f0f8f2de2dc31.gif[/img]

notes.title: Updated Roadmap for December
notes.content:
Survivors!

Following our established update schedule, we’ll be releasing a Regular Update at the end of November, followed by another Major Update in early December—yes, [b]early December[/b]—you read that correctly! :)

We’ve also updated the official Roadmap with information on December’s update.

First, the November update brings numerous bug fixes, tweaks, and smaller QoL improvements. We’ve especially focused on balancing Radiation, as it has caused a lot of trouble recently. The session start has also been reworked for better immersion and world-building, not to mention the addition of new expeditions.

Now, on to the highlights of December’s Major Update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/864ca3c111ca12cc53f6fceccda801b11336a4c9.png[/img]
[list][*][b]Traders:[/b] Meet familiar faces from [i]Endzone - A World Apart[/i] to trade goods and take on their unique quests.
[*][b]Hunting:[/b] Wildlife now roams the world of Endzone 2, providing a new food source through newly introduced hunters.
[*][b]Electricity+:[/b] The Electricity feature is being upgraded, allowing global distribution across all zones.
[*][b]Content:[/b] Additional side missions and new expeditions will be available with the update.[/list]
We’ll share more in-depth information as the update’s release approaches. Stay tuned!

notes.title: #2 | Major Update | Electricity & Upcycling 💡 NOW LIVE
notes.content:
Survivors,

it’s time to embrace a new dawn in Endzone 2 with our first major update! This transformative update introduces powerful new technologies to your settlements. Harness the energy of the elements with Wind Turbines, Solar Power Systems, and more as you connect buildings using Power Poles and Relay Stations, igniting a new era of resource management and community growth.

But the journey doesn’t end there! Revitalize the world around you by upcycling valuable ruins, including coal and copper mines, to reclaim essential resources for your survival and jump start your efforts to restore human civilization.

Join us in this electrifying adventure as you power your settlements and define what it means to thrive in Endzone 2! The future is bright—let’s illuminate it together!

[i]Please note: Some voiceovers are still being finalized and will be added in future updates. Thank you for your understanding as we continue improving your experience.[/i]

Also, here's a visual-treat for your to enjoy: The Electricity & Upcycling Update Trailer
